operation_results.detail: Astro screenshots come from the exact candidate worktree; the consumer adapter SHA includes the partial-final-row fix discovered during this execution.
The live EventCard Large variant container still has 13 members. Both recorded anomaly shape IDs remain present and were not moved, detached or deleted.
Created an isolated linked EventCard v2 candidate with row-ratio and calendar axes. calendar=absent contains no Calendar node.
The candidate IR wording media-component-swap was refined during execution: the component link and ratio variant remain master-owned; only the content image fill is substituted per fixture.

The linked Penpot reconstruction is on the review board. The exact Astro PNG could not be uploaded through the active Penpot MCP media endpoint; the board carries an explicit blocker instead of a false screenshot placeholder.

All four cards use the same long-lived Golden Event Corpus records as the real Astro capture. Titles, occurrence, place, admission, counters, calendar state and media content were read back from linked component instances.
The review wrapper contains a linked 1180 × 1203.640625 archetype instance; its four child EventCard instances remain linked.
No quarantine mutation was attempted. The IR requires explicit owner approval; both existing anomaly IDs remain in the 13-member live container.
Read-back found 0 detached instances, 0 Penpot validation errors, exact fixture overrides in both the archetype master and linked review copy, and unchanged live membership.

All three EventCard v2 masters now place transparent feedback immediately after the dark surface and keep the 6px outer bottom inset as an explicit linked layout spacer. The partial final row uses the exact Astro-measured 528.640625px height. Both the archetype master and its review copy inherited the change; no terminal instance patch or detach was used.

Read-back found fillImage.keepAspectRatio=null on all four linked media artwork overrides. The bounded Astro/Penpot pairs confirm aspect distortion and crop-window drift. This is a media-frame treatment defect, not event content drift; it must be repaired through the linked media-frame contract/rematerialization boundary before the next export, never hidden by scaling comparison images.

This export proved the title → meta → place order and exposed the 6px feedback-baseline, partial-row-height and keepAspectRatio media drift. The geometry defects were fixed; media-frame treatment still requires a child-master/rematerialization repair. The recorded Penpot export hash is intentionally not treated as current evidence.
